description.narrative:
Huvudsyftet med kärnstödet till Biotica är föreningens institutionella utveckling och övergången från projektbaserad till en uppdragsdriven organisation. På så sätt kommer Biotica inom kärnstödet att genomföra sin strategi för perioden 2022-2025 och motsvarande ramverk för resultatbedömning. De tre viktigaste resultaten som Biotica arbetar mot är:
1) Förbättrade förutsättningar för biologisk mångfald genom återställande av ekosystem, skydd av hotade arter och främjande av hållbar utveckling. 2) Ökad motståndskraft hos samhällena från målområden; 3) Konsolidering av intern kapacitet och partnerskap.
Biotica kommer att arbeta med centrala och lokala myndigheter, akademi, företag, organisationer i det civila samhället och allmänheten för att öka förståelsen för vikten av och skyddet av den biologiska mångfalden. Biotica kommer också att genomföra småskaliga infrastrukturförbättringar av ekosystem, utarbeta och delta i samråd med utkast till rättsakter och lokala planer, utveckla relevanta studier.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution - Core support Biotica (15742)

description.narrative:
The Annual Conclusion on Performance of the support to Biotica that was made on 11 April 2023. In summary it concluded that:
Biotica has progressed in all the intended areas of the strategic plan.
The activities planned for 2022 were mostly conducted; those actions that were not done in 2022 will be done in 2023 in the planned amount. All activities contributed to the achieving of the planned indicators for 2022 of the BIOTICAs Development Strategy Outputs and contributed partly to the achievement of the planned indicators of the Outcomes. ____________________________ The Annual Conclusion on Performance registered for the the 2023 year was performed based on the partner submitted progress report. In summary can be concluded the following: The Biotica Association has put efforts in following the agreed strategic plan. During the 2023 period the partner has reached an impressive results following the agreed RAF working on development of studies and policies for improvement of conditions for Biodiversity, working with communities from rural areas on raising awareness and increase knowledge on environmental issues. Moreover, the Association has worked on the consolidation of internal capacities and partnerships. ___________________________ The results accomplished by the organisation throughout 2024 can be presented as follows: During the 2024 period, the BIOTICA NGO with financial support from Sweden has implemented activities aligned with the following three key development directions: improved conditions for biodiversity, raised resilience of communities in target areas, and consolidation of internal capacities and partnerships.
The key outcomes accomplished in each area during the 2024 period are as follows:
1. Improved conditions for biodiversity by rehabilitation of ecosystems, safeguarding endangered and rare species, and promotion of sustainable development (with a focus on target areas):
- Biodiversity research on rare plants in their natural habitats conducted. -In partnership with Arnika NGO (Czech Republic), a pilot methodology was developed for mapping key species in preparation for the Natura 2000 network in Moldova. - Draft law on protective forest belts elaborated together with the analysis of the regulation impact for the Law on protective forest belts and submitted to the Ministry of Environment. - Draft regulation on the environmental voluntary inspector. - In 2024, BIOTICA contributed to enhancing ecosystem resilience through afforestation efforts on 2.5 hectares in Cîrneni village (Causeni district). Other planting trees events took place in Iagorlic Reserve, Talmaza and Rsciei villages, Old Orhei. - Five winter feeding stations were installed in the Lower Dniester National Park (in the Grdina Turceasc Reserve, the Lunca Talmaza core area, and near Rsciei and Purcari) to support deer populations. - Additionally, two natural springsin the Lower Dniester National Park (near the villages of Vioara and Grdinia)were cleaned and restored. - A study tour was organized in the Czech Republic, bringing together 16 participants from Moldova. - Representatives from state institutions, protected areas, NGOs, and volunteer inspector groups visited four protected areas, a sustainably managed commercial forest, and one of the largest river revitalization projects in the country.
2. Raised resilience of communities from the target areas.
- During the 2024 period, BIOTICA facilitated working group meetings in all villages surrounding the Lower Dniester National Park, with approximately two meetings held in each location. These sessions provided a forum for citizens to discuss the next steps following the establishment of the national park, address ongoing challenges, and propose viable solutions. Additionally, participants contributed to identifying priority measures needed to enhance the environmental conditions and improve access to social infrastructure for local communities. - In 2024, Tudora village undertook a community-driven initiative to improve local living conditions by organizing and securing the village landfill. The effort included site cleanup, tree planting, and the installation of 300 posts with 600 meters of fencing, effectively preventing waste spread and enhancing the area's ecological state. - A visitor point in Purcari was constructed, providing facilities for both local residents and visitors. - Several awareness-raising activities were organized in 2024 to educate the population on environmental issues, biodiversity, and related topics. - In 2024, in collaboration with local group in Tudora village, BIOTICA developed a new local strategy focused also on environmental protection. - The nursery managed by Samas-Plant company, benefited from the equipment, which includes a motor pump, irrigation filter, and water reservoir, is used for the drip irrigation of seedlings sown in spring, as well as for poplar and willow seedlings.
3. Consolidation of internal capacities and partnerships
- In 2024, BIOTICAs nine-member teamcomprising five men and four womenactively participated in several training programs aimed at strengthening their technical expertise. One session, conducted by Propark Romania, focused on developing ecological reconstruction plans for forests, meadows, and water bodies. Additionally, a team member attended a training organized by e-Circular that covered environmental compliance, including steps for obtaining environmental authorization, assessing environmental impacts, and crafting pollution prevention plans for enterprises. The staff also joined a workshop led by Czech expert Peter Roth, exploring the international methodology for establishing NATURA 2000 sites. - During the 2024, the Biotica has implemented measures to strengthen financial control. Additionaly, the organisation worked on improving its visibility in society through various means, such as active presence on social media, conducting arround 20 awareness campaigns and participation in local and national events, conferences, and forums on environment topic. - Biotica continued to actively strengthening partnerships with various organizations and institutions in 2024.
There are several risks which are still relevant for the last years, such as the war in Ukraine, staff fluctuations and local public authorities lack of staff which delays their analysis and approval of draft regulations and other relevant documents. Another risk included in the Development Strategy was low interest of locals for environmental issues. Especially due to the price increase of food and services, the local population and authorities became a little more interested in environmental issues.
Several important lessons emerged during the implementation of activities. Building strong cooperation with local public authorities proved essential for achieving successful outcomes, requiring continuous information exchange and active involvement in both project execution and decision-making. It also became clear that coordinating initiatives in protected areas can be time-consuming, particularly when theres no established procedure for approving new types of activities. Delays were experienced in obtaining environmental permitsespecially for sewage system installations in village institutionsdue to a lack of clarity and extensive requirements from the Agency of Environment. As a result, future planning should account for longer timelines and include thorough preparation to meet documentation and compliance needs.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
